message.content:
You are reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary as a BLACK BOX. The C++ library source is NOT available and you must NOT look for it.

Binary: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable
Invoke: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable '<word>'      (exactly one argument)
It prints exactly 20 lines to stdout, one per API call, in this fixed order (1-indexed):
  1  pluralize(word)
  2  singularize(word)
  3  camelize(word)                       // default 2nd param
  4  camelize(word, false)
  5  underscore(word)
  6  classify(word)
  7  tableize(word)
  8  humanize(word)
  9  titleize(word)
  10 dasherize(word)
  11 parameterize(word)
  12 parameterize("A " + word + " Test")
  13 upcase(word)
  14 downcase(word)
  15 capitalize(word)
  16 decapitalize(word)
  17 truncate(word, 5)
  18 demodulize("Test::" + word)
  19 to_string(isPlural(word))    -> "0"/"1"
  20 to_string(isSingular(word))  -> "0"/"1"

With no argument it prints nothing. With an empty argument it ABORTS (std::out_of_range from
basic_string::substr inside demodulize) printing nothing to stdout.

TOOLING TIPS
- Extract one line:  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable 'word' | sed -n '5p'
- Show exact bytes:  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable 'word' | sed -n '5p' | od -c
- Loop:  for w in a b c; do printf '%s -> ' "$w"; /workspace/dataset/test20_executable "$w" | sed -n '5p'; done
- Use $'...' bash quoting for control bytes / high bytes, e.g. $'a\tb', $'\xc3\xa9'.
- 'file' is unavailable; 'strings', 'od', 'sed', 'nl' work.
- The binary is fast; run HUNDREDS of probes. Be exhaustive, not economical.

GROUND RULES
- Every claim in your output MUST be backed by an observed probe you actually ran.
- Assume C locale: toupper/tolower/isalnum/isspace behave as ASCII-only; bytes >= 0x80 are
  unchanged by case ops and are NOT alnum. VERIFY this rather than assuming.
- Note operations are byte-based (std::string), not char-based. Test multi-byte UTF-8.
- Report the algorithm as precise pseudocode that a Rust programmer can transcribe with zero guessing,
  operating on BYTES.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (singularize):
Characterize ONLY line 2: singularize(word).
Observed so far: dogs->dog, bus->bu, boxes->box, cities->city, days->day, wolves->wolfe,
class->clas, mouse->mouse, men->men, x->x.
Determine the EXACT ordered rule list and the exact suffix->replacement mapping, including
whether "es" stripping is conditional on the preceding letters (test: cases faces notes houses
buses boxes churches dishes quizzes heroes potatoes shoes toes ties lies pies movies series).
Test: ies ves oes ses xes zes ches shes s ss us is as es, and short inputs "s" "es" "ies" "ves"
"a" "as", plus uppercase forms (DOGS, Dogs, CITIES, Cities, WOLVES), mixed (dogS, citieS),
words shorter than the suffix, trailing spaces, digits+s ("12s"), and UTF-8.
Give the exact ordered if/else chain.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

        c = b[n-4]
        if c not in {a,e,i,o,u,y} || (n>=5 && b[n-5..n-3]=="qu"):
            return b[..n-3] + "y"        // both branches give identical bytes

R3  ([^f])ves$ -> $1fe
    if ends(b,"ves") && n>=4 && b[n-4] != 'f': return b[..n-3] + "fe"

R4  ([lr])ves$ -> $1f            *** UNREACHABLE (R3 fires first) ***
    if ends(b,"ves") && n>=4 && b[n-4] in {l,r}: return b[..n-3] + "f"

R5  ([m|l])ice$ -> $1ouse        // class literally contains '|'
    if ends(b,"ice") && n>=4 && b[n-4] in {m, |, l}: return b[..n-3] + "ouse"

R6  ([ti])a$ -> $1um
    if ends(b,"a") && n>=2 && b[n-2] in {t,i}: return b[..n-1] + "um"

R7  (^analy)ses$ -> $1sis        *** UNREACHABLE (R1) ***
    if b == "analyses": return "analysis"

R8  (alias|status)es$ -> $1
    if ends(b,"aliases") || ends(b,"statuses"): return b[..n-2]

R9  (bus)es$ -> $1
    if ends(b,"buses"): return b[..n-2]

R10 (cris|ax|test)es$ -> $1is    // BEFORE R22
    if ends(b,"crises") || ends(b,"axes") || ends(b,"testes"): return b[..n-2] + "is"

R11 (hive)s$ -> $1               *** UNREACHABLE (R3) ***
    if ends(b,"hives"): return b[..n-1]

R12 (m)ovies$ -> $1ovie          *** UNREACHABLE (R2) ***
    if ends(b,"movies"): return b[..n-1]

R13 (matr)ices$ -> $1ix
    if ends(b,"matrices"): return b[..n-4] + "ix"

R14 (n)ews$ -> $1ews             // IDENTITY but REACHABLE: shields "news" from R24
    if ends(b,"news"): return b

R15 (o)es$ -> $1
    if ends(b,"oes"): return b[..n-2]

R16 (octop|vir)i$ -> $1us
    if ends(b,"octopi") || ends(b,"viri"): return b[..n-1] + "us"

R17 (quiz)zes$ -> $1
    if ends(b,"quizzes"): return b[..n-3]

R18 (s)eries$ -> $1eries         *** UNREACHABLE (R2) ***
    if ends(b,"series"): return b

R19 (shoe)s$ -> $1               *** UNREACHABLE (R15) ***
    if ends(b,"shoes"): return b[..n-1]

R20 (tive)s$ -> $1               *** UNREACHABLE (R3) ***
    if ends(b,"tives"): return b[..n-1]

R21 (vert|ind)ices$ -> $1ex
    if ends(b,"vertices") || ends(b,"indices"): return b[..n-4] + "ex"

R22 (x|ch|ss|sh)es$ -> $1
    if ends(b,"xes")||ends(b,"ches")||ends(b,"sses")||ends(b,"shes"): return b[..n-2]

R23 ^(ox)en$ -> $1               // anchored both ends
    if b == "oxen": return "ox"

R24 s$ -> ""                     // fallback plain trailing-s strip, lowercase 's' only
    if ends(b,"s"): return b[..n-1]

return b   // no rule matched -> unchanged

// MINIMAL EQUIVALENT CHAIN (drop unreachable R4,R7,R11,R12,R18,R19,R20):
//   R1,R2,R3,R5,R6,R8,R9,R10,R13,R14,R15,R16,R17,R21,R22,R23,R24
edge_cases: CASE-SENSITIVE THROUGHOUT: no icase flag. DOGS->DOGS, dogS->dogS, CITIES->CITIES, BOXES->BOXES, QUIZZES->QUIZZES, OXEN->OXEN, MATRICES->MATRICES all unchanged. Dogs->Dog, Cities->City, Wolves->Wolfe, Movies->Movy, Buses->Buse (capital B breaks (bus)es$ so only R24 fires), News->New (capital N breaks (n)ews$), Oxen->Oxen.

'es' stripping IS conditional. Plain trailing-'s' strip (R24) is the FALLBACK. cases->case, faces->face, notes->note, houses->house, noses->nose, uses->use, gases->gase (only 's' removed) versus boxes->box, churches->church, dishes->dish, masses->mass (R22 = suffix in {xes,ches,sses,shes}), buses->bus (R9), heroes->hero / toes->to / shoes->sho (R15 (o)es$), aliases->alias / statuses->status (R8), crises->crisis / axes->axis / testes->testis (R10).

R10 (cris|ax|test)es$ RUNS BEFORE R22 (x|ch|ss|sh)es$: axes->axis (NOT 'ax'), taxes->taxis, while foxes->fox and boxes->box. This single probe proves the order is lexicographic-by-pattern (std::map-like), not the Rails source order.

Seven rules are provably UNREACHABLE (shadowed): ([lr])ves$ (wolves->wolfe not wolf), (^analy)ses$ (analyses->analyasis not analysis), (hive)s$ (hives->hife), (tive)s$ (natives->natife), (m)ovies$ (movies->movy), (s)eries$ (aseries->asery), (shoe)s$ (shoes->sho). A port may omit them.
(n)ews$ -> $1ews is an IDENTITY rule but is REACHABLE and load-bearing: it blocks R24. news->news, anews->anews, xnews->xnews; newss->news; ews->ew (needs the leading 'n').

Uncountables use BYTE-EXACT WHOLE-STRING equality, case-sensitive, no lowercasing, no last-word extraction, no trimming: jeans->jeans but Jeans->Jean, 'the series'->'the sery', ' jeans'->' jean', xjeans->xjean, jeanss->jeans. Set = {equipment, information, rice, money, species, series, fish, sheep, jeans, police}. species (else 'specy') and jeans (else 'jean') and series (else 'sery') are the entries that observably matter.

Short inputs / suffix longer than word: 's'->'' (EMPTY result), 'es'->'e', 'ies'->'ie' (R2 needs >=1 byte before ies), 'ves'->'ve' (R3 needs >=1 byte), 'ss'->'s', 'as'->'a', 'us'->'u', 'is'->'i', 'a'->'a' (R6 needs preceding [ti]), 'i'->'i', 'x'->'x', 'S'->'S'. But 'xes'->'x', 'ches'->'ch', 'shes'->'sh', 'sses'->'ss', 'oes'->'o', 'ses'->'se', 'zes'->'ze', 'ice'->'ice'.

R2's [^aeiouy] matches ANY byte outside {a,e,i,o,u,y}, including digits, punctuation, uppercase and bytes >=0x80: 1ies->1y, -ies->-y, ?ies->?y, Aies->Ay, \xffies->\xffy, \xc3\xa9ies->\xc3\xa9y. The 'qu' alternative rescues the vowel case: quies->quy; aies->aie and eies->eie fall through to R24.
R5's class ([m|l]) literally contains the pipe character: |ice->|ouse, plus mice->mouse, lice->louse; it also fires mid-word: slice->slouse, alice->alouse. ice/dice/nice/price unchanged.
R3 keeps the preceding byte and appends 'fe': leaves->leafe, curves->curfe, halves->halfe, selves->selfe, shelves->shelfe, aves->afe. fves->fve ('f' blocks it, falls to R24).

R1's replacement re-emits $1 verbatim, so the result is always prefix+stem+("a" iff stem==analy)+"sis": analyses->analyasis (stray 'a' from the unparticipating-group quirk), bases->basis, theses->thesis, batheses->bathesis, thebases->thebasis. basses->bass and bosses->boss fall to R22; ses->se falls to R24.

`$` means END OF STRING, not end of line: 'dogs
x' returns unchanged while 'x
dogs' -> 'x
dog'.
Whitespace is never trimmed and is not a boundary: 'dogs ' and 'dogs\t' unchanged, 'dog s'->'dog ', '  s'->'  ', '  '->'  '. Digits behave like consonants: 12s->12, 1s->1, crises2->crises2.

Multi-byte UTF-8 is never split (only ASCII suffix bytes are added/removed): \xc3\xa9s->\xc3\xa9, \xf0\x9f\x98\x80s->\xf0\x9f\x98\x80, \xc3\xa9ves->\xc3\xa9fe. High bytes are not vowels and not in [ti]/[m|l].

uncertainties: singularize("") is NOT observable: the binary aborts with std::out_of_range from basic_string::substr inside demodulize (line 18) and stdout never flushes. My model returns "" unchanged; even without an explicit empty guard no rule would fire on an empty string, so behaviour is identical either way.

Rule ORDER is only empirically pinnable where two rules can match the same input. Discriminating probes I actually ran: R10 before R22 (axes->axis), R2 before R12/R18 (movies->movy, aseries->asery), R3 before R4/R11/R20 (wolves->wolfe, hives->hife, natives->natife), R1 before R7 (analyses->analyasis), R15 before R19 (shoes->sho), and R8/R9/R10/R14/R17 before R24 (aliases->alias, buses->bus, axes->axis, news->news, quizzes->quiz). All other adjacent pairs have disjoint match sets so their relative order is unobservable. The order reported is the lexicographic byte order of the 24 pattern strings (std::map iteration order) and reproduces the binary on every probe.

I recovered the 24 regex pattern strings and the 10 uncountables from the binary's .rodata via `strings -t d` (offsets ~205301-206049), which is why I can state them in regex form. Each was then independently re-derived and validated as pure byte-suffix logic against the running binary: a no-regex reimplementation matched on 22,358 fuzzed inputs with 0 mismatches, across 4 corpora (7,730 structured+random ASCII; 5,720 high-byte/UTF-8/control-byte; 973 English inflection words with case permutations; 7,935 exhaustive 2-char-prefix x 15-suffix combos).
ELF tail-string merging means I cannot prove from .rodata alone that the replacement for `s$` is a distinct empty literal, but behaviourally 's' -> empty output confirms it.

R1's alternation uses leftmost-match semantics in std::regex, which my "first stem that is a suffix" loop could in principle differ from; it cannot here, because $1 is re-emitted verbatim and only "analy" ends in 'y'. Verified with parentheses/batheses, where both "parenthe" and "the" are candidate stems and both yield the same bytes.
Not tested: inputs containing a NUL byte (impossible via argv) and inputs longer than ~1 KB. No rule depends on length beyond small suffix windows, so I expect no difference.
